auditor_value: v = 2√2 m/s ≈ 2.83 m/s at 45° to the initial velocity; s = √5 m ≈ 2.24 m at 26.57° to the initial velocity

findings.quote: Using ω = at² for displacement instead of ½at² gives s⊥ = 2 m instead of 1 m.
findings.note: ω is the symbol for angular velocity, not displacement; the perpendicular displacement is s⊥. The numbers named are right, but the printed symbol is wrong and a student copying it would write an angular quantity for a length.
findings.fix: Using s⊥ = at² for the perpendicular displacement instead of ½at² gives 2 m instead of 1 m.
